summary: Toru Kumeji works in Buddhist studies. He has held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and at the Humanities Information Studies Institute, where he was attested as senior researcher in 2015.

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, and founded the Koreanology Association. He was a professor at Keijo Imperial University (~1926–1945), Fukuoka University (~1947–1950), and Tenri University (~1950–1965).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, where he was an assistant in 1998, later holding senior researcher posts at two humanities institutes.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982, studying under Karl Hoffmann and others. He later served as professor at Osaka University and Tohoku University.
Toshihide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. In 1995, he held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Keio University and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Keio University (~1937–1969), McGill University (~1969–1979), and Komazawa University.

Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He held posts at Tokai Gakuin University, Tohoku University, and Shitennoji University.
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as an associate professor and held a post at Nagoya University from ~1990 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, later serving as professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Toshikazu Watanabe specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He has held appointments at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and Kokugakuin University.

Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology, having studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977). He served as professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020) and at Kyoto University of the Arts (~2020).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts as professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019) and Kacho Junior College, and directed a manuscript research institute.
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1928 to 1931. He held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1957–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2008) and held researcher appointments at Toyo University (~2013–2021) and Zhejiang University (~2017).

Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1952–1969) and later worked at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1969–1978).
Toshio Sako specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University, where Alex Wayman was his doctoral supervisor.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and Hannan University, and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977) and Chuo University (~1977–1987).
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor in Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).
Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Enryo Inoue (~1890–1893) and Seiran Ouchi, and later held a post at Nihon University.

Tou-hui Fok (1940–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at New Asia College, Otani University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he also lectured from ~1972 to 1988.
